regime_context: The detector shows a defensive, crowded health-pharma leadership structure: Big Pharma is the headline theme (eligible, trend-healthy, breadth 1.0, crowded), with adjacent defensive themes (healthcare EW, defensives, staples) also eligible, trend-trending, and crowded. Rotation is narrowing (19/49 eligible) with no one-narrative and no coherent directional handoff — the validated edge is the absolute-trend gate, and headline leadership is coincident concentration, not a return forecast.
emerging_watch: Watching 'Defensives' (unscorable, XLP/XLU proxy) as the purest defensive composite: if Consumer Staples EW holds its trend-gate and the broader defensive cohort maintains breadth above 0.9 while AI/tech ranks continue to decay, that would confirm a defensive leadership structure worth leaning into beyond single sectors. I would retire this watch if staples or healthcare EW lose their trend-gate eligibility and breadth drops below 0.7 within three weeks.

theses.subject: Big Pharma
theses.thesis: Big Pharma is the only high-durability, full-breadth, trend-confirming theme that is both eligible and headline. The absolute-trend gate (the validated drawdown-control leg) is satisfied, durability_bar is high, hurst is trend, and breadth is 1.0. Crowding (z=1.46, crowded=true) is a size-down caution only, not a fade. Given the track record (dir_accuracy 0.413, hit_rate 0.565), the lean is modest.
evidence: crowded=true but only a down-size flag
theses.dissent: Crowded thematic leadership in pharma can mean attention-flow is already priced — the detector's own guardrails warn that attention spikes mark tops, and rank alone has ~0 forward IC.

falsifier.text: PPH gives back its trailing 10-day relative gain and closes below its 50-day average before the check-by date

theses.subject: Health Care (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Health Care EW is a second eligible, trend-durable defensive leg with near-full breadth and high crowding. If the Big Pharma thesis is directionally right on defensive leadership, equal-weight healthcare gives a cleaner sector expression with the trend-gate satisfied. Crowding (z=1.54) again argues for sizing-down, not adding.
theses.dissent: The theme overlaps heavily with Big Pharma leadership and is equally crowded — this may be one defensive bet expressed twice rather than independent confirmation.

falsifier.text: XLV falls more than 4% relative to the S&P 500 and loses its 50-day average before the check-by date

theses.subject: Consumer Staples (Equal-Weight)
theses.thesis: Staples EW is another eligible trend-confirming defensive leg with high breadth and the highest crowding_z in the top group (1.89). It fits the broad defensive-leadership structure but the crowding is the strongest caution signal of the cohort — a continuation lean only with explicit down-sizing.
theses.dissent: Extreme overcrowding in a low-growth sector means any macro rotation toward risk could unwind this leg fast — and the detector provides no timing edge for that.

falsifier.text: XLP underperforms the S&P 500 by 5% over the hold horizon before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
